raw_response:
I've been growing cotton on this land for decades. Three mu, just me, and a well. I know what works here in Quzhou.

I'm not going to change much this year. At my age, I don't have the energy to experiment. I've watched neighbors try new things and lose money. I plant what I know.

I'll use hybrid cotton seed — I switched to it years ago because the yields are better than the old varieties and the extension station distributes them. I know how to handle it now.

For fertilizer, I put down base fertilizer before planting — compound fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium — and then top-dress with urea during the boll-setting stage. I've been doing this for years and it gives me a good boll. I won't over-fertilize because it just wastes money and makes the plants too leafy.

My well gives me water when I need it. I'll irrigate at seedling stage, flowering, boll expansion, and one more if it gets dry in August. Four times is usually enough. Last year I did four and it was fine.

Pesticide — cotton here gets aphids and bollworm every year without fail. I'll spray about six times from June through August. I know the timing by now.

I'll do rotary tillage before planting. Ploughing is too hard on my body now.
